events.excerpt: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto The Justice Department and Europol said Thursday that Operation TorNado has produced 354 arrests and the seizure of more than $234 million in cash and virtual currencies, in what the FBI called the largest takedown yet of dark web drug vendors and buyers. The announcement came from the department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement team, or JCODE, an FBI-led group created in 2018. Officials said Operation TorNado is the sixth, and most extensive, internationally coordinated action since then, and that it builds on last year’s Operation RapTor. The sweep ran from May 2025 to October 2026. Europol, which coordinated work with agencies in 14 countries, published a parallel statement the same day. The operation targeted vendors and buyers who had been active on five dark web markets already seized by law enforcement: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. Officials also identified accounts on DrugHub and on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services. The seizures included about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, among them fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and MDMA, plus 38 pill presses and 209 firearms.
events.headline: DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto

events.excerpt: Hi all, Happy to launch private.zecblock.com , a version of ZecBlock where the server doesn’t learn what you look up. ZecBlock Private uses PIR (Private Information Retrieval) . How it works Your browser encrypts the search before sending it. The transaction ID, block or address never leaves your device in readable form. The server works through the whole dataset to answer, without knowing which record you asked for. It sends back one encrypted answer, and only your browser can decrypt it. A search for something that exists looks the same as a search for something that doesn’t. As far as we know, it’s the first full block explorer (transactions, blocks and addresses) built on PIR. Previous PIR explorer demos covered narrower lookups, such as address balances. Check it yourself Open your browser’s developer tools (Inspect → Network) and search for something. Every request of the same kind is the same size, and none of them contains what you typed. After each search, the site also shows a short summary of exactly what your browser sent. Details Data stays close to the chain tip: new blocks are published every few seconds, typically within about 20 seconds of the regular explorer. Each data publication is signed, and your browser checks every result against it. Searches are heavier
events.headline: ZecBlock Private: look up transactions, blocks and addresses with PIR

Or navigating the dark forest without turning on all the lights TL;DR: In a private system we cannot know who holds voting power, how many people sit behind it, or whom they are connected to. The answer is not to abolish the privacy. It is to bound what any vote can decide, so that capturing one voting mechanism cannot confer control over the whole system. Part 1: An Ode to Rough Consensus . Part 2: When We Disagree: Making Rough Consensus Work . Zcash is building a parallel financial system, outside of but adjacent to the existing one. Its governance, however, remains entirely inside human institutions. That private financial system starts from a different assumption from the one we have become accustomed to elsewhere: privacy is normal. Dark pools let large investors trade without displaying their orders, so that others cannot trade against them. Dark does not mean lawless. events.excerpt: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Says It Has Fully Covered the $6.34 Billion Hack With Company Funds Binance said Thursday it has completed coverage of the $6.34 billion Oct. 29 hack from company funds, two weeks after the largest crypto theft on record, even as withdrawals continue to reopen in phases. In a Thursday announcement, the exchange wrote that it “has completed coverage of assets impacted in the security incident” and published a new proof-of-reserves snapshot. It repeated the same message on X. That wording matters. Coverage means Binance has replaced the affected tokens from its own books, not that it has recovered the stolen coins from the attackers. The exchange said it committed more than $6.34 billion in company funds and bought the affected tokens through market and over-the-counter channels, drawing on a partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a portion of its futures insurance fund above the level required under its risk-management framework, and its corporate treasury. Binance has also committed to replenishing SAFU to about $1 billion after that partial draw, a step it said would keep the fund fully resourced as an emergency user-protection reserve. events.excerpt: Description A few small nit cleanups on the synchronizer component in consensus. Behavior change: fetch_blocks_from_peers now returns as soon as no request is in flight, instead of idling until the 4s FETCH_FROM_PEERS_TIMEOUT. This affects two cases: no request was sent because every selected block was already locked, or the last outstanding request failed with no peer left to retry on. In both cases no further network request is sent, and a failed request still waits the full 2s request timeout, so periodic runs cannot repeat faster than every ~2s on failures. The only new cost is local: while all selected blocks are locked, the scheduler polls get_missing_blocks at its default 200ms cadence instead of every 4s, which is the same cadence it already uses during fast successful sync. Added a test covering both cases. Test plan CI/PT Release notes Check each box that your changes affect. If none of the boxes relate to your changes, release notes aren't required. For each box you select, include information after the relevant heading that describes the impact of your changes that a user might notice and any actions they must take to implement updates. Protocol: Nodes (Validators and Full nodes): gRPC: JSON-RPC: GraphQL: CLI: Rust SDK: Indexing Framework: Co-authored-by: Claude Fable

events.excerpt: Bitcoin Magazine Israel Discount Bank to Let Customers Trade Bitcoin in App Starting Nov. 26 Israel Discount Bank said Wednesday that from Nov. 26 it will let eligible customers buy, hold and sell bitcoin and ether in the bank’s mobile app, a launch that would beat larger rival Bank Leumi if it stays on schedule. The Tel Aviv-listed lender described the service as a first for Israel’s banking system in a Nov. 11 statement. Customers will be able to trade the two assets alongside stocks and bonds, without opening an account at an outside exchange or managing a separate digital wallet. The offer is limited to private, not corporate, customers who are Israeli residents, 18 or older, and whose accounts are already set up for securities trading, subject to the bank’s terms. “For the first time in the banking system, Discount Bank will allow trading in digital currencies directly from the bank account in a simple and secure manner, without the need for complex dedicated digital wallets,” Avi Levi, CEO of Discount Group, said in the statement. “This is a first step toward establishing advanced technological infrastructure in the digital currency space and developing the bank’s capabilities in this area.” The rollout was led by Elad Fisher, head of the bank’s financial markets division.
events.headline: Israel Discount Bank to Let Customers Trade Bitcoin in App Starting Nov. 26

events.excerpt: Summary This proposal introduces post-quantum signature aggregation with leanVM in shadow mode . BLS remains the only authority for aggregates: consensus validity depends on BLS alone, exactly as today. leanVM aggregates and proofs are produced and verified alongside BLS, but their results have no effect on consensus. They are only measured, compared, and reported. When PQ/AI day arrives, an emergency hard fork simply retires BLS and enables leanVM in full. By “PQ/AI day” we mean the point at which quantum computers, or AI-assisted cryptanalysis, make BLS unsafe to rely on. Motivation Ethereum has to be ready for post-quantum signatures well before BLS is actually broken. Waiting until the last moment would mean deploying new, complex code to mainnet in a hurry. Giving leanVM authority early has its own risk: leanVM is new code that hasn’t been tested in production. However carefully it is built and audited, we can’t rule out a soundness bug that accepts an invalid proof, or a liveness bug that rejects a valid one. The main benefit of shadow mode is that Ethereum isn’t put at risk from a leanVM bug before PQ/AI day arrives. Because leanVM has no authority, a leanVM bug can’t break Ethereum’s security or halt the chain. At the same time, leanVM runs on mainnet under real load, so
events.headline: EIP Draft: Run leanVM aggregation in shadow mode alongside BLS until PQ/AI day
